## Design

### 2026-10-09: This is basically my first time making something in KiCad for the purposes of actually putting it into a PCB. I've done some tutorials and used it to make general schematics, but nothing to the precis

**2.12h**

This is basically my first time making something in KiCad for the purposes of actually putting it into a PCB. I've done some tutorials and used it to make general schematics, but nothing to the precision of a thing that should be assembled.

Although I was thinking of using the AtTiny85, I don't think it has enough IO for my purpose. I switched to the more powerful CH32V003, that should have plenty for my needs. I also learned more about Charlieplexing to power all the LEDs.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 135944](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/69e97716b0d67c6fb8b54c0aa3799848ac9a07e0c826da0731f0d5d31af7c1b8.png)

What I need to get down now is the proper placement on the PCB footprint, get accurate silkscreens.

I think I will also leave space to incorporate usb-c power, so I'll need a good way to switch between power from usb, from a cell battery, or to be off.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/dd6bc46a-0815-4d59-a0dd-4f174cd13918/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11: I have started arranging the different components roughly onto the PCB.

**1.57h**

I have started arranging the different components roughly onto the PCB.

I haven't yet incorporated usb-c power, and I want to maybe make it more compact so it can act as a business card.
I think a double throw switch could be used for switching between power? I still haven't decided if I wanted to add the ability for both.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/0ecb6772-c975-4701-90c8-828b2ea27279/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11: Wow being able to puzzle through all the connections reuqired was really fun, fixing the minor bugs that arose because of the footprints after realizing it wasn't my fault was a great usage of my time

**2.33h**

Wow being able to puzzle through all the connections reuqired was really fun, fixing the minor bugs that arose because of the footprints after realizing it wasn't my fault was a great usage of my time.

I also got some silkscreen elements added to make it a bit more personalized, with a ruler on the front and a qr code on the back to my github. Everything just about feels ready

### 2026-10-26: There were a whole lot of inconsistencies between the schematic and the chosen footprint, since I mostly just went based on vibes the first time. This time, I actually looked through different product

**1.63h**

There were a whole lot of inconsistencies between the schematic and the chosen footprint, since I mostly just went based on vibes the first time. This time, I actually looked through different product descriptions and tried to find what would be most available given the manufacturers.

It is also at this point that I realized that I apprently had chosen some rare components which would either just not be available, or add significant costs if I wanted to order and/or get the board assembled.

![Screenshot 2026-10-25 234430](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/30ede43f5416d7c68ade83f0891cd123229e2af2dd223510bbd774b0c0fc2483.png)

I also got to work in making it so the smd components are on the top, and anything that is through hole could be hand soldered by myself afterwards.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/01d84a60-8451-4156-8eba-ac61d3373eea/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-26: JLCPCB's assembly would not let me place the accelerometer with the plan I was with, so I decided to look for alternatives online. Generally they would have similar problems or increase costs, so I de

**2.8h**

JLCPCB's assembly would not let me place the accelerometer with the plan I was with, so I decided to look for alternatives online. Generally they would have similar problems or increase costs, so I decided to use the same board as a breakout board so I could solder the connections manually.

This also gave me the opportunity to learn how to create my own footprints and decide what is necessary to keep

![Screenshot 2026-10-26 150503](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Xt10ZK7FTi1vKiU37U67a1QQj2rKZWIn/9c597fd931a1b636da113857474b2d6ffc4d45baa40b0243e34a39674d90e930.png)

During the change of footprints and moving traces along a lot of what the traces got messy so I decided to  go back and redo parts that looked like they may cause problems. I updated the BOM to match, and I think I just need to make the final preparations and optimizations before submission.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/7df394e3-f8ea-4c53-95cc-2ec891018bf5/video.mp4)
